text:
Rita Gomez: Heads-up: SI partner "Aurora Systems" flagged a failure during their marketplace install in a gov-region PoC. asking for an architecture review + escalation.
Tom Baker: what failed exactly?
Rita Gomez: image signed and pulled, but the runtime can't bind GPUs — kernel module fails on node init. their infra team suspects our marketplace image is missing the vendor driver shim.
Eve Li: is this a marketplace packaging bug or an environment mismatch? which node/os?
Rita Gomez: Ubuntu 22.04 GKE-like node image, NVIDIA driver 535. they see dmesg: "nvidia: probe failed - unknown symbol".
Markus Vogel: hmm could be we ship a precompiled kernel module expecting different kernel ABI. did MarketplaceBot record the image build metadata?
MarketplaceBot: image: redwood/inference-marketplace:2026-03-18-rc3, build-id: bld-9042, kernel-headers: 5.15.0-88, signature: sha256:abcd...
Tom Baker: we need the exact host kernel version and whether DKMS was used. ask Aurora to paste /proc/version and uname -a.
Rita Gomez: asked, they posted uname: "Linux node-1 5.15.0-102-gov #1 SMP Thu Mar 19 18:02:22 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux".
Eve Li: mismatch: image was built against headers 5.15.0-88, host is 5.15.0-102. two options: provide a DKMS-friendly module or publish a new marketplace image compiled against 5.15.0-102. DKMS path preferred for PoC.
Markus Vogel: for security/regulatory reasons they can't install unsigned kernel objects. our module must be signed with partner-approved cert OR we use a userspace fallback (cuda-container-runtime) if possible.
Rita Gomez: legal asked for note: if we sign modules for customer, need SLA addendum. tagging LegalQA.
LegalQA: acknowledged. we'll review but will need partner consent form.
Tom Baker: immediate next steps: 1) ask Aurora to confirm if they can load signed module; 2) provide a DKMS tarball signed by our build key; 3) offer a no-kernel fallback (run on CPU emulation or use NVIDIA container runtime) as temporary.
Eve Li: I can build a DKMS package and sign it. can we keep this scoped to PoC (not prod)? build will take ~6 hours.
Rita Gomez: timeline note: Aurora wants greenlight for internal go/no-go on Fri. we have 48 hours.
MarketplaceBot: INC-3890 opened: marketplace-gov-kmod-fail. priority=P1. assigned: eng-runtime, partnerships.
Markus Vogel: also checklist for Aurora pre-checks: kernel headers present, secureboot status, modprobe logs, and whether they enforce module signature. request tcpdump or journalctl excerpt.
Tom Baker: I'll schedule a 30m emergency arch review tomorrow 09:30 PT with Aurora Eng, their infra/security lead, Eve, Markus, and me. invite sent.
Rita Gomez: can someone draft a short runbook for the SI to run so we don't do live debugging? Aurora prefers runbook first.
Eve Li: I'll drop a step-by-step: checks, DKMS install commands, verify modinfo, and a fallback container launch. will post link.
Rita Gomez: thanks. also note: marketing said the partner announcement is on hold until the PoC can boot GPUs. please escalate. :warning:
Markus Vogel: operational note: if secureboot prevents unsigned modules, the DKMS package must be signed with a key the host trusts or we need to enable MOK enrollment. both are heavy for gov deployments. mention both in runbook.
Tom Baker: good point. include commands for 'sudo mokutil --sb-state' and enrollment steps with caveats.
Rita Gomez: Aurora replied: they cannot perform MOK enrollment for gov compliance. they asked if we can provide an alternative path.
Eve Li: alternative is deliver a containerized runtime that avoids kernel modules — we can ship a user-space runtime that interfaces with GPUs via a supported container runtime (if their node image has vendor GPU support enabled). ask for lsmod and /proc/driver/nvidia/version.
MarketPlaceBot: aurora supplied lsmod: empty for nvidia, /proc/driver/nvidia not present.
Tom Baker: ok assume no vendor support. Plan: Eve builds DKMS signed module for host kernel 5.15.0-102 and we provide a signed MOK key they can import via their compliance process, or we publish a special 'gov' marketplace image compiled for their kernel.
Rita Gomez: LegalQA please prioritize the consent form so we can sign modules if needed.
LegalQA: will escalate and aim for draft within 24 hours.
Eve Li: posting runbook draft: <link.internal/runbooks/aurora-gov-kmod-runbook.pdf>. contains commands, expected outputs, and escalation contacts.
Tom Baker: after tomorrow's triage I'll post minutes and an action tracker. we need to hit Aurora's Fri deadline.
Markus Vogel: if we can't resolve kernel signing by Fri, prepare a contingency: partner covers 2 days of eng time for a custom image rebuild. flag to partnerships for billing.
Rita Gomez: noted. I'll confirm commercial fallback and hold announcement until PoC green.
MarketplaceBot: INC-3890 updated: triage scheduled, attachments: runbook-draft.
Tom Baker: thanks all — please add any pre-reads here.
Eve Li: :hammer_and_wrench: I'll start the DKMS build now and post artifacts to the runbook link.
Rita Gomez: closing for now, will reopen if Aurora raises new blockers after triage.
